chunks: From him, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Al-Husayn ibn Salim Al-Ijli, that Al-Washy was brought to him.

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَالِمٍ: Al-Husayn ibn Salim, a companion of Imam Al-Sadiq (AS).
key_terms.الْعِجْلِيُّ: Al-Ijli, the nisba indicating Al-Husayn ibn Salim's tribal or regional origin.
key_terms.الْوَشْيُ: Al-Washy, a specific companion of the Imams often cited in narrations.
key_terms.يُونُسَ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ: Yunus ibn Yaqub, a prominent narrator in the Four Books.

ai.seo_question: Who was Al-Washy and what is his connection to Al-Husayn ibn Salim in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi highlights the scholarly practice of verifying reports (al-washy) through trusted companions like Al-Husayn ibn Salim, who served as a key link in transmitting Imam al-Sadiq's teachings. It underscores the rigorous chain-of-transmission methodology in Shia hadith sciences, where the authenticity of a report is often confirmed by presenting it to a reliable narrator for validation.
